# Synthesized Code Review — PR #172
**Branch:** feat/issue-162-cli-entry-points-delete-ts-wrappers
**Date:** 2026-04-25
**Review Type:** Multi-model synthesis (Claude Sonnet 4.6 + GPT 5.4 + Gemini 3.1 Pro)
**Base:** development

---

## Synthesis Overview

PR #172 introduces Python-native CLI entry points (`story-writer tui | run | resume`) via `pyproject.toml` and deletes all 18 legacy TypeScript tool wrappers from `.opencode/tools/`. The three models reached near-unanimous agreement on the release-blocking packaging error, but diverged significantly on secondary issues: GPT surfaced the most findings (1 Critical, 3 Warnings), Claude focused on correctness and testing gaps (1 Critical, 2 Warnings, 2 Suggestions), and Gemini uniquely identified a tool-coupling regression in the agent prompt files (2 Criticals, 1 Suggestion). Independent verification confirms the build backend error as well as the stale tool references in `prompts/agents/story-orchestrator.md` and the non-functional `--savepoint` selection, elevating several singular findings to genuine. The PR is not ready to merge.

**Model Agreement Score:** 6/10 — unanimous on the top blocker; moderate divergence on everything else.

## Consensus Findings

### ★★★ Unanimous Findings (All Three Models Agree)

```
[U-C-01] Invalid setuptools build backend — entry point can never be installed
Severity: Critical
Category: Correctness
File: pyproject.toml
Lines: 3
Detail: build-backend = "setuptools.backends.legacy:build" is not a valid PEP 517
  setuptools backend. The correct values are "setuptools.build_meta" or (for legacy
  compatibility) "setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__". As declared, pip immediately
  aborts with a BackendUnavailable / ModuleNotFoundError before any build step runs,
  meaning the [project.scripts] console script "story-writer" can never be
  installed. Claude verified against setuptools 78.1.1; Gemini notes the expectation
  of a legacy setup.py that also does not exist; GPT confirms wheel builds fail.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✓  Gemini ✓
Suggestion: Change pyproject.toml line 3 to:
    build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
  Optionally add package discovery config so the installed namespace is consistent
  with in-source imports (see [M-W-04] / [S-I-01]).
```

---

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

```
[M-W-01] --batch flag is documented as a mode switch but is a permanent no-op
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness
File: src/presentation/cli/main.py, src/presentation/cli/argument_parser.py
Lines: main.py 36–49; argument_parser.py (--batch help string)
Detail: _cmd_run() accepts batch but immediately discards it (_ = batch) and always
  constructs NullApprovalGate(). run_pipeline() derives batch_mode from
  isinstance(gate, NullApprovalGate), so "story-writer run" runs headless regardless
  of --batch. docs/tools.md line 95 correctly documents this as a forward-compat
  placeholder, but the argparse help text still reads "Auto-accept all approval gates
  (non-interactive)" with no caveat — users running "story-writer run --help" receive
  a description that implies distinct behaviour. GPT classifies this as Warning;
  Claude classified it as Suggestion, noting the pipeline outcome is identical.
Models: Claude ✓ (Suggestion)  GPT ✓ (Warning)  Gemini ✗
Dissenting view: Gemini did not surface this finding. Given docs/tools.md already
  documents the no-op intent, the remaining gap is solely the argparse help string.
  This synthesiser rates it Warning — the CLI is the user-facing surface and the
  help text misleads.
Suggestion: Update the --batch help string in argument_parser.py to note the current
  no-op status, e.g.: "Auto-accept all approval gates (no-op; interactive mode not
  yet implemented — flag retained for forward compatibility)."
```

```
[M-W-02] tui subcommand is exposed but permanently non-functional
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness / Testing
File: src/presentation/cli/main.py, tests/unit/test_cli_main.py
Lines: main.py 17–31; tests (general)
Detail: GPT and Claude both flagged the tui subcommand from different angles. GPT
  (W-03) notes that src/presentation/tui/ does not exist in the repository, so
  _cmd_tui() always falls into the ImportError branch and exits with status 1 —
  making this a permanently non-functional command on this branch. Claude (W-02)
  notes the complementary testing gap: TestMainDispatch covers run and resume
  dispatch paths but has no test for the tui subcommand. Verification confirmed that
  .opencode/tools/ only contains .gitkeep and no TUI package exists in src/.
Models: Claude ✓ (testing gap)  GPT ✓ (always fails)  Gemini ✗
Dissenting view: Gemini did not raise this finding. The tui command's graceful
  ImportError + SystemExit(1) behaviour appears intentional (documented in
  docs/tools.md line 91), but shipping an exit-1 command without a test verifying
  the failure mode is the gap. And the argparse registration invites users to
  try a command that will never succeed on this branch.
Suggestion: (a) Add a test verifying that "story-writer tui --story x" raises
  SystemExit(1) and emits the expected error message to stderr. (b) Consider
  gating tui registration behind a runtime check or optional extra so the help
  output does not advertise a command that always fails.
```

### ★☆☆ Singular Findings (Only One Model Reported)

```
[S-C-01] Agent prompt files reference deleted TypeScript tool names
Severity: Critical (Gemini) — verified genuine
Category: Correctness
File: prompts/agents/story-orchestrator.md (and likely other agent .md files)
Lines: story-orchestrator.md lines 334–349 (## Tools section)
Detail: Gemini (C-02) claimed that deleting the TS wrappers without updating
  opencode.json and agent prompt files leaves the OpenCode runtime broken.
  Independent verification partially confirms this. The opencode.json file is clean
  — it contains no tools arrays and was not incorrectly claimed. However,
  prompts/agents/story-orchestrator.md contains a full ## Tools section listing 16
  named tools (story-state, savepoint-mgr, critique-runner, scene-writer, etc.) that
  were provided by the now-deleted .opencode/tools/*.ts wrappers. The agent prompt
  explicitly instructs the orchestrator: "Always invoke pipeline operations through
  the named OpenCode tools listed in the Tools section below. Never shell out to
  python3 src/tools/*.py." With all TS wrappers deleted, the OpenCode agent is
  instructed to use tools that no longer exist.
  Nuance: this only affects the legacy OpenCode agent-based workflow. The new
  story-writer CLI (the subject of this PR) does not use these prompts at runtime.
  If the OpenCode agent workflow is being retired, the residual risk is lower — but
  the prompts are still present and would break any user invoking the agent directly.
Model: Gemini only
Assessment: Genuine finding, verified. Classification downgraded from the full scope
  Gemini described (opencode.json is clean), but the agent .md file issue is real.
  Gemini's framing of the opencode.json "permissions block" as a citation is
  [unverified] and incorrect — no tool arrays exist there. The agent .md finding
  stands on its own merit after direct verification.
```

```
[S-W-01] --savepoint accepted but ignored for actual savepoint selection
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness
File: src/presentation/orchestrator.py, src/presentation/cli/main.py
Lines: orchestrator.py 336–363; main.py 50–63
Detail: GPT (W-02) identified that _cmd_resume() forwards savepoint_name to
  resume_pipeline(), but the implementation calls _load_savepoint(story_name) with
  no savepoint selector — it always loads the single latest pipeline_state.json.
  The savepoint_name argument is only used to validate membership in
  state.savepoints, raising StoryGenerationError if the name is not found. A user
  providing a specific savepoint name to resume from gets no meaningful behaviour
  change; they always resume from the latest checkpoint. This is silent misbehaviour
  since no error is raised when a valid name is passed. Verified directly against
  orchestrator.py:336–363 and _load_savepoint signature at line 45.
Model: GPT only
Assessment: Genuine finding, verified. The CLI advertises targeted resume; the
  backend does not implement it. Given the savepoint validation gate prevents a
  crash with valid names, this degrades silently.
```

```
[S-W-02] sys.path mutation executes at import time, not invocation time
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness
File: src/presentation/cli/main.py
Lines: 9–14
Detail: Claude (W-01) correctly observes that the sys.path.insert() calls at lines
  9–14 run unconditionally at module import time — during test collection and any
  import of main.py, not only when story-writer is invoked. For non-editable
  installs, __file__ resolves to site-packages, and parents[3] yields a high-level
  site-packages directory rather than the project root. The path surgery is correct
  for editable installs (current dev workflow) but fragile if install mode changes.
  Secondary concern: the current pyproject.toml uses parents[3] for a very shallow
  package depth assumption that could break if the module is relocated.
Model: Claude only
Assessment: Genuine finding, verified against main.py lines 9–14. The editable
  install mitigates it in practice today, but this is a latent bug waiting for
  the install mode to change. Worth fixing in tandem with [U-C-01].
```

```
[S-I-01] Dual module identity: src.presentation.* and presentation.* coexist
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Style
File: src/presentation/cli/main.py, pyproject.toml
Lines: main.py 9–14, 40–43; pyproject.toml:10
Detail: Claude (S-01) notes that [project.scripts] declares
  src.presentation.cli.main:main (using the src. prefix) while in-module imports
  use from presentation.cli.argument_parser (no src. prefix), relying on the
  sys.path hack. Both names resolve to the same file but are distinct Python module
  objects. This is harmless in this call chain but violates src-layout conventions
  and would cause isinstance() failures across the boundary.
Model: Claude only
Assessment: Genuine architectural concern. Fixable by configuring
  [tool.setuptools.packages.find] where = ["src"] and updating the scripts entry
  point to presentation.cli.main:main, which also eliminates the sys.path hack.
```

```
[S-I-02] docs/tools.md Pipeline CLI section lacks prose subsections per subcommand
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Documentation
File: docs/tools.md
Lines: 79–95
Detail: Gemini (S-01) flags that the new ### Pipeline CLI section provides a
  reference table for tui, run, and resume but no per-subcommand ### prose
  subsections. Verification confirms the table exists at line 87–93 with one
  implementation note. The --batch no-op context is covered by the note (line 95).
  The gap is limited: no separate subsections elaborate on parameter behaviour or
  expected output. The --savepoint limitation (see [S-W-01]) is also not documented
  here.
Model: Gemini only
Assessment: Valid style suggestion. The more actionable improvement is adding a note
  about --savepoint's current limitation (always loads latest state) rather than
  restructuring into prose subsections.
```

## Divergence Analysis

```
[D-01] Severity of --batch no-op
GPT says: Warning — the parser help text advertises a mode switch that doesn't exist
Claude says: Suggestion — "the pipeline outcome is identical with or without the flag"
Gemini says: Not raised
Assessment: GPT is more precise. The distinction matters because users inspect
  --help output to make decisions; a misleading help string is more than cosmetic.
  docs/tools.md already documents the intent correctly, which partially supports
  Claude's lower severity. Synthesiser has elevated to Warning given the argparse
  help string is the primary user-facing documentation for CLI users.
Resolution: Classified as [M-W-01] at Warning severity.
```

```
[D-02] Nature of the tui concern
GPT says: Correctness issue — the command always exits with status 1; should not be
  registered until the TUI module exists
Claude says: Testing gap only — the dispatch path is not covered in TestMainDispatch
Gemini says: Not raised
Assessment: Both are correct views of the same underlying situation. GPT's framing
  captures the user-visible problem; Claude's captures the test coverage gap.
  The synthesised finding [M-W-02] incorporates both angles. GPT's recommendation
  to gate registration is the stronger fix, but Claude's test addition is an
  independent improvement.
Resolution: Combined into [M-W-02] with both corrective actions noted.
```

```
[D-03] Scope of tool-coupling violation
Gemini says: Both opencode.json and agent prompts contain stale references to deleted
  tools (Critical)
Claude says: Not raised
GPT says: Not raised
Assessment: Gemini's finding is partially misattributed. opencode.json has no tools
  arrays — no stale tool names there. However, prompts/agents/story-orchestrator.md
  lines 334–349 does list 16 tool names that correspond to deleted TS wrappers, and
  this was independently verified. The opencode.json claim is [unverified] and
  incorrect; the agent prompt claim is verified and genuine.
Resolution: Classified as [S-C-01] (Singular), with severity noted as Critical-
  potential but scoped to OpenCode agent-based workflow only.
```
